title: Freedom
lead: Freedom is a central idea in Galatians: 'For freedom Christ has set us free' (Galatians 5:1). Paul sets the free woman against the slave woman, the child against the slave, and the Gentile believer's freedom from circumcision against the 'slavery' of those who would impose it. In Scripture the standard picture of freedom is the Exodus, where God freed a slave people.

sections.b: The Exodus is the model of freedom: God brought Israel out of slavery (Exodus 20:2). The law of release in the seventh year and the Jubilee freed slaves (Exodus 21:2; Leviticus 25:10). Paul speaks of freedom from sin (Romans 6:18), from the law (Romans 7:3-6; Galatians 5:1) and from death (Romans 8:21), and warns that freedom is not an excuse for the flesh (Galatians 5:13). Jesus says that the Son frees (John 8:36).
